lede: Your kidneys filter the blood and decide how much water goes back into it, which is what keeps the amount of water in your body steady. Everything else about water is fixed, so the volume of urine is the part that changes.
can: Name the parts of the excretory system and say what each does.
List three ways water is gained and three ways it is lost.
Give the direction of ADH: more ADH, less urine, more concentrated.

text: The kidney, water balance and ADH

md: Drink a litre of water and within an hour you need the toilet; sweat through a hot afternoon and you barely go at all. Your kidneys are filtering the blood and deciding how much water to keep.

explain: The kidney. The bladder only stores the urine until it is released — Summer 2025 examiners reported bladder being given here.

md:
**The names, in order.** Blood arrives through the **renal artery** and leaves through the **renal vein**. The **kidney** filters it and makes urine. Each kidney's urine runs down a **ureter** to the **bladder**, which stores it, and it leaves the body through the **urethra**.
**Ureter and urethra** are one letter apart and mean different things. The ureter carries urine **down** from the kidney; the urethra carries it **out**. Summer 2024's examiners were explicit that a spelling had to be near enough to be told apart from the other word.

prompt: Which tube carries urine from a kidney to the bladder?
explain: The ureter. The urethra carries urine out of the body, and the renal vein carries blood, not urine.

md: Cut a kidney in half and you see three regions the specification names: the **cortex** on the outside, the **medulla** inside it, and the **pelvis**, the space where urine collects before it enters the ureter. The outcome says in as many words that **no detail of the nephron is needed** — so glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and the loop of Henlé are not on this paper.

title: GCSE Biology Revision "The Kidneys" (Triple)
why: The structure of the kidney and what it does to the blood. It goes further into the nephron than CCEA needs — watch it for the filtering and reabsorption idea, then answer the question underneath.

prompt: Which region of the kidney is on the outside?
explain: Cortex outside, medulla inside, pelvis in the middle where the urine collects.

alt: Two boxes. The left box, water gained, lists water in food, water in drink and water made by respiration. The right box, water lost, lists evaporation of sweat, evaporation during breathing and urine produced by the kidney. Arrows run between the two boxes.
svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 760 280" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-labelledby="k153t"><title id="k153t">The three ways water is gained by the body and the three ways it is lost</title><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4"><rect x="20" y="60" width="300" height="170" rx="8"/><rect x="440" y="60" width="300" height="170" rx="8"/><path d="M356 128 h68" marker-end="url(#k153)"/><path d="M424 172 h-68" marker-end="url(#k153)"/></g><defs><marker id="k153" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L10 5 L0 10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12.5" fill="currentColor" font-weight="600"><text x="34" y="86">Water gained</text><text x="454" y="86">Water lost</text></g><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12.5" fill="currentColor"><text x="34" y="120">in food</text><text x="34" y="152">in drink</text><text x="34" y="184">made by respiration</text><text x="454" y="120">evaporation of sweat</text><text x="454" y="152">evaporation during breathing</text><text x="454" y="184">urine produced by the kidney</text></g><g font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="currentColor"><text x="20" y="32">Three in, three out — and the kidney is the only one of the six the body can adjust.</text><text x="34" y="216" font-size="11.5">respiration: glucose + oxygen → energy + CO₂ + water</text><text x="454" y="216" font-size="11.5">the kidney controls how much water is reabsorbed</text><text x="20" y="266" font-size="11.5">Summer 2025: candidates gave sweating as a route of water loss, but fewer also said breathing out.</text></g></svg>
caption: Three gains, three losses. Only one of the six can be adjusted.

md:
**Gained:** in **food**, in **drink**, and **made by respiration** — the water on the product side of the respiration equation is real water the body keeps.
**Lost:** by **evaporation of sweat**, by **evaporation during breathing** (which is why a cold window mists up), and as **urine** produced by the kidney.
Only the last of the six is under control. The kidney **filters the blood** and then **controls how much water is reabsorbed**, so the volume of urine is what changes when the balance shifts.

prompt: Which is the third way the body gains water?
explain: Respiration makes water as a product, and the body keeps it.

title: Summer 2025 B1 Foundation Q8 and B1 Higher Q3
md: Asked which organ produces urine, **quite a few candidates stated the bladder**. On the graph, some **read 120 instead of 110**, and others **read the wrong student's line**. Asked which student had lost the most water by other routes, quite a few named the right student but **fewer explained that they had produced the least urine**. And on the final part, **sweating** was given but **fewer also said breathing out**.

title: Why urine volume is the only tap the body can turn
md: Of the six routes water takes, five are fixed: you cannot decide how much your food holds, how much respiration makes, or how much evaporates. Only the kidney can be told to put water back.

prompt: Besides sweating and urine, name the third way the body loses water.
answer: breathing | breathing out | evaporation during breathing | exhalation
explain: Evaporation during breathing. Summer 2025 examiners reported that candidates gave sweating but fewer also gave breathing out.

md: **Reading a urine table.** If a student produced 20, 30, 40, 50 cm³ at the four check times, the **total** is 140 cm³ — add, do not average. The student who produces the **least** urine is the one who has lost the most water by the other two routes, and that comparison is what earns the explanation mark.

prompt: A student produced 20, 30, 40, 50 cm³ of urine at the four check times. What was the total volume, in cm³?
explain: 20 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 140 cm³. Add all four; the question asks for the total, not the mean.

title: One sentence, learnt in one direction
md: **ADH causes the kidney to reabsorb more water, so less urine is produced.** ADH is a hormone, so it is made by a gland, travels in the **blood** and acts on its target organ, the **kidney**. More ADH → more water reabsorbed → **less** urine, and the urine is more **concentrated**. Negative feedback is not required by the outcome, so you do not need the full loop — but you do need the direction.

prompt: A person has been running in hot weather and has sweated a lot. What happens to their ADH?
options: More ADH is released, so less urine is produced
Less ADH is released, so more urine is produced
ADH is unchanged, because sweating is not the kidney's job
answer: More ADH is released, so less urine is produced
explain: Sweating removes water from the blood, so the body holds on to what is left: more ADH, more water reabsorbed, less urine.

prompt: Someone drinks two litres of water quickly. What happens to the volume and concentration of their urine?
options: A larger volume of more dilute urine
A smaller volume of more concentrated urine
The same volume, but more concentrated
answer: A larger volume of more dilute urine
explain: Too much water in the blood means less ADH, so less water is reabsorbed: more urine, and more dilute.

md:
Name the **kidney, ureter, bladder** and **urethra** and say what each does.
Name the **cortex, medulla** and **pelvis**.
List three ways water is **gained** and three ways it is **lost**.
Explain how the kidney changes **reabsorption**.
Give the direction of **ADH**: more ADH, less urine.

Summer 2025 made this the last question on both tiers, worth eleven marks: the organ named, a graph reading with a calculation, a total from a table, a bar to complete, a student identified and explained, and two other routes of water loss. Higher adds ADH. Stuck: give the explanation as well as the letter.
